name: MUFFLE FURNACE
desc: Premium Heavy-Duty Laboratory Muffle Furnace designed for high-temperature thermal processing, ashing, and material testing up to 1200°C. Features a 13-liter internal capacity, built with high-grade Kanthal A1 heating elements and a highly responsive R-Type thermocouple.
principle: The INNOLAB INSTRUMENTS MUFFLE FURNACE is engineered for precise high-temperature thermal processing up to 1200°C, employing Kanthal A1 heating elements and an R-type thermocouple governed by a microprocessor PID controller. It enables gravimetric ashing, loss on ignition, calcination, and heat treatment of ceramics, metals, polymers, coal, food, pharmaceutical, and environmental samples. Doctors, B.Sc/M.Sc students, PhD researchers, and chemists rely on it for sulfate ash and residue on ignition per USP/Ph. Eur., coal ash per ISO 1171, plastic ash per ISO 3451, and loss on ignition per ASTM D7348; it is also used to remove volatile organic compounds (VOCs), incinerate biological tissues, and sinter ceramic powders. Its double-walled ceramic-fiber insulation and triple-phase power ensure stable zone temperatures and low outer surface temperatures for reproducible high-temperature assays.
sop: Verify triple-phase 440V power connection and place the furnace on a heat-resistant bench away from flammables; inspect door insulation and chamber cleanliness.
Switch ON the main power supply; the PID digital LED display will light up.
Use the 'UP' and 'DOWN' arrows to adjust to the required target parameter (e.g., 550°C for loss-on-ignition or ash determination).
Press 'SET' again to lock the value.
Allow the PID controller to stabilize and ramp the furnace; do not open the door during ramping to avoid thermal shock.
Pre-heat the empty chamber to the target temperature for 15–30 minutes to achieve a uniform thermal profile.
Wearing heat-resistant gloves and using long tongs, place prepared sample crucibles or boats onto the ceramic hearth; distribute them evenly without touching the walls or heating elements.
Close the door securely and monitor the LED display to confirm that the process value reaches and maintains the setpoint.

After the ashing, calcination, or ignition dwell is completed, press 'SET', adjust the setpoint to a lower value if using step-down cooling, or switch OFF the heating; allow the chamber to cool below 200°C before opening the door.
Remove samples using tongs and transfer them into a desiccator to cool before gravimetric weighing or further analysis.
Once the furnace is completely cool, clean any ash residue from the chamber with a soft brush; close the door and record the process temperature and time in the laboratory logbook.

WARNING: Never open the furnace door above 200°C or when samples may release flammable VOCs; ensure organic solvents and moisture are fully evaporated or pre-carbonized before loading, and always wear heat-resistant gloves and face protection to prevent severe burns and toxic fume exposure.
